title: Connected component preimages under maps with quotient topology
statement: Let $P,W$ be topological spaces and $h:P\to W$ a continuous map. Assume that $W$ has the quotient topology for $h$, in the explicit sense that for every subset $A\subseteq W$, $A$ is closed if and only if $h^{-1}(A)$ is closed. Suppose that every fibre $h^{-1}(\{w\})$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], in particular nonempty. For a point $x$ of a space $T$, write $\operatorname{Comp}_T(x)$ for its connected component, the maximal nonempty connected subset containing $x$. Then for every $a\in P$ one has $$h^{-1}(\operatorname{Comp}_W(h(a)))=\operatorname{Comp}_P(a).$$ No compactness, separation, local connectedness or nonemptiness hypothesis on $P,W$ is imposed.
